name: after-effects-mcp
description: Build and animate compositions in Adobe After Effects, and render frames back to check the result.
long_description:
Drives Adobe After Effects through ExtendScript, using the scripting bridge that ships with After Effects itself — no panel or extension to install inside AE.

Covers projects, compositions, layers, keyframes, expressions, effects and rendering, plus a raw ExtendScript escape hatch for anything the typed tools don't reach. `ae_save_frame` renders a frame and returns it as an image, so Claude can look at what it built instead of assuming an edit landed.

Every mutating tool opens its own undo group, so anything Claude does is one undo away.

**Requires After Effects to be running.** On macOS the first call raises a system prompt asking to allow control of After Effects, which must be approved. On both platforms, *Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network* must be enabled in After Effects' Scripting & Expressions settings.

ae_app.title: After Effects application
ae_app.description: Only needed when several versions of After Effects are installed, or when it is installed somewhere unusual. On Windows, the full path to AfterFX.exe (for example C:\\Program Files\\Adobe\\Adobe After Effects 2026\\Support Files\\AfterFX.exe). On macOS, the application name (for example "Adobe After Effects 2025") or a full path to the .app. Leave blank to auto-detect.
